import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 734

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/734](https://www.erdosproblems.com/734)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [dBEr48] de Bruijn, N. G. and Erdős, P., On a combinatorial problem. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch.,
  Proc. (1948), 1277--1279 = Indagationes Math. 10, 421--423.
-/

namespace Erdos734

open Filter Asymptotics

/--
Find, for all large $n$, a non-trivial pairwise balanced block design $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq
\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that, for all $t$, there are $O(n^{1/2})$ many $i$ such that $\lvert
A_i\rvert=t$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_734 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∃ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), H.IsPairwiseBalancedDesign ∧
      (∀ e ∈ H, e.card < n) ∧ ∀ t : ℕ,
        ({e ∈ H | e.card = t}.card : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.sqrt n := by
  sorry

end Erdos734

reformulations.difference: The imported design predicate explicitly requires every block to have cardinality at least two. The website’s abbreviated definition mentions only unique coverage of every pair.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: From a witness satisfying pair coverage and the theorem’s other conditions, delete every block of cardinality less than two. Such blocks contain no two-element subset, so unique pair coverage is preserved. Properness of the remaining blocks is preserved, and the number of blocks of every size can only decrease. Conversely, the imported predicate implies pair coverage directly. Thus adding the minimum-block-size condition leaves the existential problem unchanged, with the same constant and cutoff. The corresponding full asymptotic equivalence was proved in the scratch file.

sources_consulted: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-16.pdf — Erdős, On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved, §VI.2, paragraph beginning “Prove that there is a pairwise balanced block design”.
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1948-01.pdf — de Bruijn and Erdős, On a combinatorial problem, Theorem 1 and its proof.
http://web.archive.org/web/20260709212033id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/734 — archived cited problem page, including its statement, remarks, references and open status.
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/ and https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html — bibliography used to locate both cited papers.
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/README.md — provenance of the community status database.
review.notes: Checked the sole declaration against both primary references and the archived problem page. The constant is uniform in n and t, the design is chosen before quantifying over t, and the finite-set representation preserves indexed block counts because blocks of size at least two cannot repeat under unique pair coverage. Scratch proofs and computations in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully: they verify pair-coverage equivalence, full-block exclusion, empty-family behavior, zero counts outside the permitted size range, and small cases n = 0,…,4. Nontrivial designs exist for every n ≥ 3, so the design conditions are not vacuous. The archived page and currently retrieved community database both record the problem as open. Direct live-page access remained Cloudflare-blocked, so live-site status was not independently confirmed. The reviewed file matches its committed bytes.
